A_target.statement:
Let $f: \Bbb S^n \to \R^n$ be a [[Definition:Continuous Mapping (Topology)|continuous mapping]].
Then there exists $x \in \Bbb S^n$ such that:
:$\map f x = \map f {-x}$

B_source.statement:
Let $T$ be a [[Definition:Triangulation|triangulation]] of the [[Definition:Closed Ball|$n$-ball]] which is [[Definition:Antipodal Map|antipodally]] symmetric on its [[Definition:Boundary (Topology)|boundary]].
Let $\lambda: \map V T \to \set {\pm 1, \ldots, \pm n}$ be a labelling with $\map \lambda {-v} = -\map \lambda v$ for boundary [[Definition:Vertex of Graph|vertices]] $v$.
Then there exists an [[Definition:Edge of Graph|edge]] $\set {u, v}$ of $T$ such that:
:$\map \lambda u = -\map \lambda v$

substitutions.the simplicial triangulation: a sequence of triangulations with mesh tending to zero
substitutions.the antipodal labelling rule: the sign pattern of the coordinates of f
substitutions.the complementary edge: a pair of nearby points with opposite-sign images

object_map.reformulation: The continuous statement is first re-expressed as the vanishing of the odd map g(x) = f(x) - f(-x), which is what the sign labelling discretizes.

validity_conditions: f must be continuous so that sign patterns are locally stable under refinement
the triangulations must be antipodally symmetric at every mesh size
compactness of S^n is needed to extract a convergent subsequence of complementary edges
proof_plan: Fix a [[Definition:Triangulation|triangulation]] $T_k$ of $\Bbb S^n$ of [[Definition:Mesh of Triangulation|mesh]] at most $\dfrac 1 k$ which is symmetric under $x \mapsto -x$.

{{AimForCont}} $\map f x \ne \map f {-x}$ for all $x$.
Let $\map g x = \map f x - \map f {-x}$.
Label each vertex $v$ by $\pm i$, where $i$ is an index maximizing $\size {\map {g_i} v}$ and the sign is that of $\map {g_i} v$.

As $\map g {-v} = -\map g v$, the labelling is antipodal.
The closed upper hemisphere is an $n$-ball whose induced triangulation is antipodally symmetric on its boundary $\Bbb S^{n - 1}$.
By [[Tucker's Lemma]] applied there, there is an edge $\set {u_k, v_k}$ with complementary labels.
As $\Bbb S^n$ is [[Definition:Compact Space|compact]], a [[Definition:Subsequence|subsequence]] of the edge midpoints converges to some $x \in \Bbb S^n$ as $k \to \infty$.

Passing to a further subsequence, $u_k$ carries the label $+i$ and $v_k$ the label $-i$ for a fixed $i$.
By [[Definition:Continuous Mapping (Topology)|continuity]], $\map {g_i} x \ge \norm {\map g x}_\infty$ and $-\map {g_i} x \ge \norm {\map g x}_\infty$.
Hence $\map g x = 0$, that is, $\map f x = \map f {-x}$.
{{qed}}
